title: Remitly vs. Wise for Nepal: Compare Fees, Exchange Rates, and NPR Delivered From the USA [2026]
summary: Compare Remitly vs. Wise for sending money from the US to Nepal. See how fees, exchange rates, and total NPR delivered stack up based on pricing data.
body_text: If you are comparing Remitly vs. Wise for sending money to Nepal from the United States , one question matters most: how many Nepalese rupees does your recipient get? That’s the figure most people care about. It helps cover rent, school fees, groceries, and everyday support for loved ones in Nepal. While transfer fees and exchange rates both matter, the clearest way to compare providers is to look at the final NPR delivered. Both Remitly and Wise help people in the United States send money to Nepal, and both show costs before you confirm a transfer. While Wise showed a slightly stronger exchange rate (rate) in our testing, Remitly’s lower fees resulted in more Nepalese rupees being delivered to recipients across every transfer amount we reviewed. Keep reading for our pricing comparison table, full methodology, and results. Quick answer: Remitly vs. Wise for USD-to-NPR Transfers Based on transfers of $500 and above paid by bank account (ACH) and sent via bank deposit. Exchange rates and fees are subject to change. Your amount at the time of sending may differ. Sending Money to Nepal with Remitly Remitly is designed to help people send money internationally in a way that’s simple, secure, and flexible. From the United States, you can send money to Nepal using debit card, credit card, bank account (ACH), Apple Pay, Google Pay, Remitly wallet balance, and pay-over-time (loan). Your recipient may be able to receive money through bank deposit, money pickup, mobile wallet . That range of delivery options can be helpful when convenience matters. Depending on the payment and delivery methods selected, some transfers may qualify for instant delivery, while others can take longer. Remitly’s stated range is instant to 3–6 business days.* For people in the United States sending money to family or friends in Nepal, Remitly is a practical option for everyday needs such as household support, rent, education costs, and medical expenses. *Transfer speed is an estimate depending on factors including payment and delivery method, subject to banking partner operating hours and availability, local laws/regulations, and compliance requirements. Sending Money to Nepal with Wise Wise is widely known for using the mid-market rate, which is the midpoint between the buy and sell prices in the wholesale interbank market. Some people may prefer to see this rate when they search online for a currency pair. However, it’s important to remember that exchange rates alone don’t tell the whole story, and focusing on just the rate rather than the total amount received after fees and charges can be misleading. For transfers from the United States to Nepal, Wise supports delivery via local bank account. Remitly vs. Wise: USD to NPR Exchange Rate vs. Fee When people compare money transfer services, they often focus on the rate first. If fees were the same across providers, that would make sense. However, Wise and Remitly use different fee structures, so a more complete comparison looks at the total amount paid and the total amount received rather than the rate alone. The total cost of an international transfer usually comes down to two things: the rate ( how many NPR each USD converts to ) and the transfer fee (the amount paid before the money is converted). In the live transfer prices we reviewed on July 21, 2026, Wise showed a slightly higher rate. However, Remitly’s fees were lower, and that difference led to a better result for the recipient: more NPR. In every tested example, more was delivered with Remitly. Compare the final amount your recipient receives. How to Compare Live Amounts Between Remitly and Wise Before You Send Money to Nepal Before you confirm a transfer, both Remitly and Wise let you review the total amount your recipient will receive, in addition to rate and fee details. Here is one way to do it: enter your transfer details for USD to Nepal on both Remitly and Wise. Select the same funding and delivery method where possible. Check the fee. Check the rate. And compare the final NPR delivered. This only takes a minute, and it gives you the most useful answer. Bottom line: Who Sends More NPR From the USA to Nepal? Both Remitly and Wise offer digital transfers from the United States to Nepal and both are transparent about pricing before you send. Based on our comparison of bank account (ACH) payments for bank deposit transfers of $500 and above, Remitly delivered more Nepalese rupees to recipients in Nepal than Wise, making it the better option if your goal is to maximize the amount received. Based on live tested amounts captured on July 21, 2026, Remitly delivered more NPR than Wise at every amount tested. The reason was simple: while Wise showed a slightly better rate upfront, Remitly’s lower fees resulted in more NPR being delivered. If you are deciding between the two, start with the figure that matters most: how many Nepalese rupees your recipient gets. Methodology: How We Compared Remitly vs. Wise We compared Wise and Remitly using identical total pay-in amounts across all tested transfer scenarios ($500. $750. $1,000. $2,000. $5,000). Because Wise’s fees scale with the transfer amount, matching the total cost to the sender often required sending more through Remitly. As a result, recipients may receive more with Remitly in some cases, despite differences in exchange rates. We believe this method offers the fairest comparison because it reflects what matters most: how much the sender pays and how much the recipient receives. Wise may offer a better rate, but if Wise charges higher fees, the recipient could still receive less overall. Comparing the final NPR amount makes sure you get the best value for your transfer. title: Base44 Pricing: 2026 Guide to Plans, Credits, and Real Total Cost
summary: Key Takeaways As of July 2026, Base44 offers five pricing tiers: a free plan plus four paid plans (Starter, Builder, Pro, Elite) ranging from $16/month to $160/month when billed annually, with higher month-to-month prices up to $200/month. * The free plan includes 25 message credits and 100 integration
body_text: Key Takeaways As of July 2026, Base44 offers five pricing tiers: a free plan plus four paid plans (Starter, Builder, Pro, Elite) ranging from $16/month to $160/month when billed annually, with higher month-to-month prices up to $200/month. The free plan includes 25 message credits and 100 integration credits per month, with a daily message cap of 5 credits. Free plan refreshes happen monthly, but unused credits do not roll over. Paid plans start at $16/month (Starter) and scale through Builder ($40), Pro ($80), and Elite ($160) on annual billing - roughly 20% cheaper than monthly plan pricing. Base44 uses a credit system with two types: message credits for building and integration credits for running live apps. The Builder plan at $40/month is the recommended starting point for most serious MVP and internal tools projects, unlocking a custom domain, backend functions, and GitHub integration. All numbers reflect publicly listed pricing as of July 2026. Always verify on Base44's pricing page before buying. Base44 pricing in 2026: quick answer (checked July 2026) How much does Base44 cost? Base44 uses a credit-based subscription model combining a monthly fee with two types of credits: message and integration. The platform offers both free and paid plans with varying credit allowances, from $0 to $200/month depending on tier and billing period. On annual billing, the Starter plan costs $16/month, Builder is $40/month, Pro is $80/month, and the Elite plan is $160/month. Month-to-month, Base44's pricing tiers range from free to $200/month. Annual billing provides approximately a 20% discount compared to monthly subscriptions. This hybrid model - a monthly price plus building and integration credits - means your actual spend depends on how aggressively you build with the AI app builder and how many real users interact with your live app. Exceeding your plan's credit limits typically requires upgrading to a higher plan. This article is an independent pricing breakdown for evaluators comparing options in the ai app builder market. Base44 is frequently considered alongside tools like Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, and Jet Admin for building ai powered apps and internal tools. Base44 plans and prices at a glance (with annual billing) Base44 pricing is organized into five main plans: Free, Starter, Builder, Pro, and Elite. Choosing annual plans over month-to-month billing saves roughly 20% across every tier, which can add up substantially if you commit for a full year. Here is how each base44 plan compares: Plan Price (billed annually) Monthly price Message credits/mo Integration credits/mo Key features Best for Free $0 $0 25 100 Core features, auth, database, analytics Testing, early stage ideas Starter $16/mo ~$20/mo 100 2,000 Unlimited apps, app code edits Personal projects, hobby MVPs Builder $40/mo ~$50/mo 250 10,000 Custom domain, free domain (1 yr), GitHub integration, backend functions, AI model selection Serious MVPs, internal tools Pro $80/mo ~$100/mo 500 20,000 Early access to beta features, premium support Agencies, growing apps Elite $160/mo ~$200/mo 1,200 50,000 Priority support, dedicated assistance High-traffic production apps The main trade-offs: Free and Starter are fine for experimentation, but Builder is the first production-capable tier with a free custom domain and GitHub export. Pro and elite plans provide headroom for scaling. Yearly billing can save money - for example, the Builder plan costs $480/year instead of $600 on monthly billing, a $120 difference. How the Base44 credit system works (message vs integration credits) Base44 does not price by seats. Instead, it uses a dual credit system that governs both building and running ai apps. Understanding how credits work is essential for accurate budgeting. Message credits are consumed when prompting the AI to build or edit applications - scaffolding a new app from natural language prompts, modifying UI layouts, debugging logic, or iterating on features. Complex or longer prompts consume more credits. These message credits effectively cap how much AI-assisted development you can do per billing period. Integration credits are spent when your deployed app triggers live actions: making LLM or API calls, sending emails, generating images, processing file uploads, or running backend workflows. Standard database reads and writes generally do not consume integration credits. Each integration action typically costs one integration credit. A complex app may use 50–100 integration credits per active user monthly, depending on how AI-heavy the features are. Key behaviors to keep in mind: Credits reset each billing cycle. For the free plan, message credits reset daily (up to 5/day). For paid tiers, both message and integration credits reset monthly. Unused credits do not roll over to the next billing cycle. Over-provisioning wastes budget. When either credit type runs out mid-month, relevant functionality pauses until the next billing cycle or a plan upgrade. Plan-by-plan breakdown: what you actually get Each base44 plan bundles different credit volumes and feature access. Here is what you actually get beyond the headline plan price. Free plan: 25 message credits and 100 integration credits per month. Includes core features like authentication, database, analytics, and hosting. Best for quick tests and validating an app idea. No custom domain, limited app count, and a daily cap of 5 message credits. You can build a working app here, but credit limits will slow serious iteration. Starter plan: 100 message credits and 2,000 integration credits. The cheapest plan that unlocks unlimited apps and in-app code editing. Suited for personal projects, learning the platform, and building a personal tool or small internal utility. Still lacks backend functions and custom domain support, so it is not ideal for production apps. Builder plan: 250 message credits and 10,000 integration credits. The recommended tier for developing complex applications and real MVPs. Includes a free domain for one year, the ability to connect your own domain, backend functions, GitHub integration, and AI model selection. This is where most serious builders land. Pro plan: 500 message credits and 20,000 integration credits. Adds access to beta features, premium support, and early access to new capabilities. Designed for agencies running multiple client apps or teams with growing active users. Elite plan: 1,200 message credits and 50,000 integration credits. Highest credit ceilings, priority support, and dedicated assistance. Built for high-traffic production apps, ai platforms, and teams that need more credits without interruption. The elite plan may also offer sub-levels with adjustable credit caps. Free vs Starter: when is the free plan enough? Many evaluators wonder whether Base44's free plan is sufficient to validate the platform. The answer depends on your pace and ambitions. Both the free plan and the Starter plan include the core AI app builder, built-in database, authentication, and hosting. The difference is credit volume and feature access. The free plan's daily message credit cap (5 per day, up to 25/month) and tiny integration allotment (100/month) tend to stall progress once you start iterating seriously. Most active builders outgrow it within days rather than weeks. The Starter plan at $16/month billed annually is better suited for continuous learning, small internal utilities, and personal tools where you need enough message credits to iterate and enough integration credits to demo to a handful of users. It also unlocks app code edits and unlimited apps. Rules of thumb: If you want to build a single internal dashboard for a team of three with light usage, Starter might suffice. If you expect a public MVP with dozens of active users, or your app will trigger more than a few hundred integration calls a month, skip Starter and go straight to Builder. If you are simply exploring whether Base44 fits your workflow, the free plan is the right plan for a weekend test - but do not expect to ship complete apps on it. Builder, Pro, and Elite: production-grade Base44 plans Builder, Pro, and Elite are positioned for production apps rather than experiments. These tiers unlock capabilities that matter once you are serving real users: custom domains, backend functions, GitHub integration, and significantly higher credit ceilings. The Builder plan ($40/month billed annually) is generally the right plan for serious builders. It includes 250 message credits, 10,000 integration credits, ability to connect a custom domain, a free domain for one year, backend functions, AI model selection, and GitHub export. If you are building a working app for a client or shipping an internal tool for your team, Builder is the practical minimum. The Pro plan is essentially Builder plus more scale: 500 message credits, 20,000 integration credits, early access to beta features premium support, and suitability for agencies or teams running several apps or a single app with moderate traffic. Pro and elite plans also position you for growth without hitting hard walls mid-month. The Elite plan is the high-end option: 1,200 message credits and 50,000 integration credits, premium support, and priority handling. It is meant for high-traffic workloads and AI-first businesses deploying complex apps or mobile apps with many active users. Concrete scenarios: a SaaS MVP with hundreds of monthly active users likely needs at least Pro. An internal tool serving 10–20 staff users is usually fine on Builder. Credit usage, not seat count, is the primary cost driver at these tiers. Total cost of ownership: what actually drives your Base44 bill The list price for a base44 plan is only part of the story. Your real-world spend depends on how heavily you build with the AI, how many live users you have, and whether you rely on external APIs. Key cost drivers beyond the monthly price: Message credit burn during development. Frequent prompt-based changes, experimentation, and debugging consume message credits fast. If you are developing complex applications, you may exhaust Starter's 100 message credits before finishing a first version. Integration credit consumption from user traffic. Every time your live app makes an LLM call, sends an email, processes a file upload, or triggers an automation, it will consume integration credits. Integration credits can deplete quickly with active user interactions - especially if your app is AI-heavy. External API costs. If your app calls OpenAI, Anthropic, or transactional email providers, those vendors bill you separately. Base44's integration credits cover orchestration, not third-party usage fees. Domain renewals. Builder and above include a free custom domain for the first year on annual billing, but renewal costs after that year are your responsibility. Base44 does not charge per seat, which can be attractive for teams with many non-technical users. But heavy credit usage can still push you into a higher plan. The fact that credits do not roll over means choosing the wrong plan - either too high or too low - wastes budget. To estimate your annual budget, map expected credit usage to plan allowances. For example: a small internal tool with 10 staff using 100 integration actions each per month needs ~1,000 integration credits/month (Starter suffices). A customer-facing AI agent with 200 active users at 50 actions each needs ~10,000/month (Builder minimum). These are conservative planning assumptions, not guarantees, so always leave headroom for hidden costs you may not anticipate. Base44 pricing vs other AI app builders (and where Jet Admin fits) Base44 is one of several ai app builders using credit-based pricing. Buyers often compare it with tools like Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, and more opinionated business-app platforms like Jet Admin. In a pricing comparison, Base44's entry-level pricing is competitive. The Starter plan costs $16/month billed annually, which is cheaper than many competitors that fall in the $18–$25/month range . Base44's free plan offering 25 message credits per month also provides a genuine no-cost starting point. On the other end, Base44's Elite plan costs $160/month (or $200 monthly), which is higher than most competitors at the top tier. Strengths of Base44's pricing: a truly free plan, predictable credit bundles, and a broad feature set (database, auth, hosting, AI model selection) included in the subscription. Weaknesses: no credit rollover, limited transparency around exactly which actions cost how many integration credits, and the risk of forced upgrades when existing apps become integration-heavy. For teams primarily building data-centric internal tools, Jet Admin offers a different approach. Rather than generating an entirely new backend, Jet Admin builds secure business apps on top of existing data sources - connecting to databases like PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, BigQuery, and Snowflake, plus SaaS tools like Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, and Shopify. This can reduce vendor lock-in and simplify governance compared with a fully closed AI app builder backend. Choosing the right Base44 plan for your use case Choosing the right plan comes down to three questions: how intensively you will build with AI each month, how many active users you expect, and how critical advanced features like custom domains, GitHub export, and backend functions are to your project. Decision guide: Free: Quick tests, student experiments, validating whether Base44's plain language approach works for your app idea. Starter: Learning the platform, building small personal tools, or early stage ideas with a handful of users. Builder: The default recommendation for real MVPs, client projects, and internal tools. If you need a custom domain and stable credits, start here. Pro: Agencies managing multiple apps, or a single app with moderate traffic and a need for early access to beta capabilities. Elite: Production apps with heavy AI workloads, high user counts, or teams that cannot afford mid-month credit limits. A simple decision flow: if you are pre-idea validation, start with Free. Once you show it to real users, move to Starter. Once you need a custom domain and stable credits, go Builder. If you hit Builder's credit limits, upgrade to Pro or Elite. Always map expected message and integration credit use to plan allowances rather than just picking the cheapest plan. Picking the wrong plan costs you either in wasted budget or in stalled development when credits run out during a current billing period. Readers who primarily want to connect existing production data and build internal business apps with strict governance may also want to evaluate Jet Admin alongside Base44. Jet Admin as an alternative to Base44 for internal and business apps While Base44 focuses on AI-assisted creation of entirely new apps - front-end, backend, and database - Jet Admin is designed to build secure business apps and internal tools on top of existing data sources and SaaS tools. Jet Admin connects to databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, and others), spreadsheets (Google Sheets, Airtable), and dozens of SaaS APIs (Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Shopify, Twilio, and many more ). This can reduce data migration and vendor lock-in compared with a fully closed backend generated by an AI app builder. Jet Admin also uses AI to help scaffold interfaces, workflows, and agents, but its core value lies in orchestrating existing systems rather than relying solely on an auto-generated backend. This simplifies long-term governance, compliance, and collaboration with engineering teams. For current Jet Admin pricing details, see Jet Admin pricing directly, as exact numbers should be confirmed before comparison. Consider Jet Admin over Base44 when: You are building internal tools on top of production databases that already exist. Fine-grained permissions and deep integrations with existing systems matter more than rapid vibe-coding a net-new app. Long-term governance, audit controls, and compliance are non-negotiable requirements. Conclusion: is Base44 pricing right for your project? Base44 pricing in 2026 is transparent and mid-range for the ai app builder market. The credit system offers predictable costs at each tier, but real spend is driven more by credit consumption and external API usage than by the headline monthly price. Free and Starter tiers are primarily for evaluation and small, low-traffic apps. The Builder plan is the practical minimum for production-ready apps thanks to custom domains, backend functions, and GitHub export. Pro and Elite plans add headroom for message and integration credits plus stronger support - essential for apps with growing user bases. Before committing to annual plans, estimate realistic user behavior and app complexity. A few hundred integration calls per month is manageable on Starter or Builder, but an AI-heavy app with hundreds of active users will push you toward Pro or Elite quickly. When Base44 is a good fit - fast AI app creation, non-coders, greenfield apps - it delivers strong value. When your priority is building secure business apps on existing data with strict governance, evaluating Jet Admin alongside Base44 is worth your time. FAQ: Base44 pricing, credits, and billing Below are common questions not fully addressed above, focused on practical billing and credit details that buyers often ask before committing to a next billing cycle. How does Base44's annual billing discount actually work? Base44's annual plans reduce the effective monthly price by roughly 20% compared to paying month-to-month. For example, the Starter plan costs $16/month billed annually versus $20 on a monthly plan. Builder runs $40 versus $50, Pro is $80 versus $100, and Elite is $160 versus $200. Buyers pay for the full year up front. If Base44 supports switching from monthly to annual mid-cycle, the system typically prorates remaining time, but confirm exact details in Base44's current billing documentation . Can I downgrade or cancel my Base44 plan without losing my apps? Generally, when you cancel or downgrade, your apps and data are preserved, but access to features like higher credit allowances, custom domains, and premium support may be lost. Annual plans are usually not refunded mid-term, while a monthly plan allows more flexible cancellation at the end of the billing period. Monthly billing is safer while you are still evaluating Base44. Does Base44 offer student, startup, or nonprofit discounts? As of July 2026, Base44 does not prominently advertise student or nonprofit discounts, though some reports suggest academic email holders may receive ad-hoc discounts. Reach out directly to Base44 with details about your use case, as many SaaS vendors occasionally grant credits or reduced pricing even when not listed on their pricing page. What happens when I run out of Base44 message or integration credits? When message credits are exhausted, you cannot send new prompts to the AI app builder until the next billing cycle or a plan upgrade. When integration credits run out, live app actions that depend on integrations may fail or be throttled. Monitor your credit dashboards closely, and stage rollouts to avoid being forced into unplanned upgrades mid-month. How do Base44 credits relate to external API costs like OpenAI or email services? Base44's integration credits cover the platform's orchestration work, but they do not replace third-party vendors' own fees. Using OpenAI, transactional email services, or other external APIs will generate separate bills from those providers. Factor both Base44 subscription costs and expected external API spend into your total cost estimates, especially for AI-heavy apps making frequent LLM calls. Policies and pricing can change, so always verify current terms directly on Base44's website before making a long-term commitment.

The Special Committee has retained Solomon Partners as its financial advisor and Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP as its legal advisor to assist in connection with the strategic review process. There is no assurance or guarantee that the review process will lead to any strategic transaction. The Company and the Special Committee do not intend to provide updates unless and until a specific course of action is approved and further disclosure is deemed appropriate. Our goal is to make every customer feel their most confident and beautiful for the moments that matter most. Founded in 1996 and delivering fresh styles almost every day, Lulus uses direct customer feedback and insights to refine product offerings and elevate the customer experience. title: 3 Top Restaurant Hiring Trends in 2025: Everything You Need to Know
summary: Explore the top 3 restaurant hiring trends for 2025: more job openings, the rise of AI in recruitment, and a surge in candidates seeking management roles.
body_text: New year, new…hiring trends? Amidst the resolutions and revelations that 2025 may bring, one thing’s for certain. Restaurant hiring is moving quickly and tirelessly, and unless you’re staying ahead of the curve, you’ll get left behind. Today, we’ll be diving into top trends and actionable strategies in restaurant hiring in 2025 to make sure that this year is your best one yet. PS: Make sure you read to the end for an exclusive interview with an expert General Manager from Five Guys! Trend #1: Restaurant job openings are reaching pre-pandemic levels of opportunity While job opportunities in the restaurant industry took a steep nosedive during the pandemic, restaurant hiring is currently on the up and up. Per the National Restaurant Association , 172,500 new restaurant and bar jobs were added in 2024. ‍ While this was a decrease from the 309,000 jobs added in 2023, the total number of restaurant job openings continues to trend above pre-pandemic levels. Nation’s Restaurant News writes that “the industry is now about 1.4% above its February 2020 employment peak, equating to about 173,000 jobs above pre-pandemic levels .” It’s worth noting that these numbers aren’t evenly distributed across all segments of the food service industry. Full service restaurants, which experienced the greatest employment dip during the pandemic, continue to trend 212,000 jobs below pre-pandemic numbers. Other sectors who have yet to recover their pre-pandemic job counts include cafeterias and buffets. On the flipside, job openings at quick service restaurants, fast casual restaurants, bars, and taverns are trending higher than their pre-2020 numbers. Tailor your hiring strategy for a competitive restaurant labor market The growing number of open restaurant positions has created a competitive hiring landscape. In order to stand out and secure top quality talent, try the following tactics: Offer competitive pay and benefits: Research salaries at similar brands in your area, and be prepared to offer comparable – if not higher – rates. If you’re unable to offer higher pay, consider alternative benefits that make your company stand out, such as healthcare and support for student loans. Provide flexible scheduling options: Flexibility is a particularly compelling factor that will help you stand out in a competitive labor market. If your company has any special scheduling considerations – for example, one of our partners doesn’t require employees to work night shifts, ever – make sure to clearly state this in your job description. Trend #2: Technology is the key to hiring efficiency The advent of AI is here, and it’s here to stay. And as more and more people begin to use Chat GPT and other AI-powered tools in their daily lives, it’s no wonder that it’s slowly becoming more heavily utilized in the workplace. In the restaurant industry, specifically, “37% of operators plan to invest in automated labor management recruitment/scheduling systems in 2024” ( National Restaurant Association’s 2024 Restaurant Technology Landscape Report ). In a recent interview with Bloomberg , co-founder Eugene Remm of multi-unit icon Catch Hospitality Group, shared: “The bigger conversation is on efficiency. Ultimately, all restaurants are going to have to work with a better efficiency model, which means doing more with less…I think you really have to focus a lot on technology. So you talk about AI, and how that changes a lot of the dynamics.” While hospitality purists may resist the rising tides of technology, leveraging new tools doesn’t mean detracting from the human element of the service experience. Remm continues: “Technology is just a supplement for the team. It doesn’t replace the team. Ultimately, if you don’t have a great team you’re not going to have great gas, and then you’re not going to make the money you need to make.” It’s an important distinction to make. Technology is a tool to help your business cut down on repetitive manual tasks. What is it not ? A replacement for a high quality team that interacts with your guests and creates memorable experiences. How to leverage technology to hire better in the restaurant industry ‍ Start by writing out the areas of the hiring process that take the most time. Chances are, you’ll find that these are manual, repetitive tasks: candidate sourcing, resume vetting, and scheduling interviews, for example. Once you’ve clarified these areas, you can explore ways to invite technology into your process to save time and manual effort. Here are a few ideas: AI for Resume Vetting: Build custom parameters to bulk filter out unqualified resumes, ensuring that candidates are pre-qualified before you spend time on an interview. Chat Bots for Candidate Engagement and Interview Scheduling: Use Language learning models (LLMs) to ask additional vetting questions, schedule interviews, and send interview reminders to candidates. This allows candidates to receive an instant response – even if they’re applying to a job at 2 a.m. While it’s certainly possible to build your own AI tools and chat bot flows, 2025 is not the year to waste time. Our team of experts is working with 500+ industry-leading brands like Tao Group Hospitality, Erewhon, KFC, and Another Broken Egg Cafe to provide end-to-end AI-powered hiring support, and they’re ready to help you too. Click here for a free 30-minute consultation call with our team. Trend #3: Applicants are aiming for management positions Recently, the LANDED team spoke with Ulrich Kogda, General Manager at Five Guys in New York City, who shared about an increase in applicants with leadership goals in mind. "There are a lot of people who are understanding the potential in fast food and want to become managers and leaders, and eventually run their own stores. In 2025, we’ll be getting a lot of candidates who want to have leadership roles.” This increasing emphasis and ambition towards managerial positions is a departure from what Kogda has seen in the past. “Previously, people were coming in who just wanted to be crew members, dishwashers. Now, it’s switched over, and we’re seeing lots of applicants express that they want to learn and they want to grow.” When asked how he encourages new–and existing–hires towards the career trajectories that they aim for, Kogda responded: “Whether you’ve been here for five months or you’ve just started, I like to put everybody on the same level and encourage them to be curious, be respectful, and have a positive attitude towards everything. The admin stuff is secondary, those are skills that you learn. But personality and attitude – those aren’t things you can teach, they depend on you as an individual.” When it comes to the most crucial aspects of being a restaurant leader, Kogda solidified the importance of remaining calm and collected, and to always focus on human connection. “This is a people business, and you have to have a positive attitude no matter how many times a customer or employee may try to poke you. In order to grow in your career, you have to understand that those around you are always going to have their own emotions and feelings. You have to learn how to stay composed and react appropriately.” How to optimize your restaurant hiring process for career-oriented applicants A spike in ambitious applicants is ultimately a great thing for your restaurant, especially if you’re able to invest time and energy into helping them achieve career milestones. By hiring candidates who will grow with your company, you’ll boost retention and create a team of top performers who are invested in your brand’s success in the long term. To attract and nurture applicants with managerial goals in mind, try these strategies: Highlight opportunities for career growth in your job description: Ensure that your job description includes timelines and information about promotions. Maintain an open dialogue during and after the interview process: Keep the feedback loop going throughout the interview process and after candidates join the company. Make space for applicants to share about their career goals, and take time to help them create action plans to get to the next promotion. How to stay ahead in restaurant hiring and build your dream team Keeping these trends and tips in mind will help you hire a top-performing team for your restaurant in 2025. But as the applications begin to roll in, you may find yourself feeling swamped and overwhelmed with tedious manual admin tasks. LANDED’s end-to-end hiring solution saves managers time and money by leveraging advanced generative AI to automate routine tasks. Ready to build your dream team? Connect with us today and let LANDED help you streamline your hiring process, so you can focus on what truly matters—running a successful restaurant in 2025 and beyond.

title: The convenience of mobile banking apps over brick-and-mortar banking
summary: Have you ever wondered what the difference is between mobile banking and online banking? Even though the two terms are often used interchangeably, there are some variations between both services.
body_text: The convenience of mobile banking apps over brick-and-mortar banking Remember when you had to wait in long lines at brick-and-mortar banks just to make a deposit? Or rushing after work to get there before it closes? Yeah, we don't miss those days either. Last updated: November 27, 2024 Today, you can do all your banking transactions easily and conveniently from your phone. With a mobile banking app, you can manage your finances anytime and anywhere. These apps are designed to make your life more efficient than traditional banks. We’ll show you why you should give digital finance a try. The Rise of Mobile Banking At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, many of us stayed indoors to practice social distancing. While banks were considered essential, many people wanted to limit the places they went to. As a result, more people took advantage of the financial institution’s apps, which led to the rise of mobile banking in places like the United States. It's no surprise that more and more people are realizing the convenience of mobile banking, and this trend is expected to continue. During 2020, the World Bank reported that 40 percent of adults in low and middle-income economies who preferred in-store transactions before the pandemic now use mobile banking. Since then, transactions that took the better part of your afternoon at the bank can now take seconds with a few taps on your smartphone. As of 2023, 59% of Americans prefer mobile banking , 22% prefer online transactions, and only 19% still prefer bank visits. Mobile banking vs online banking: What's the difference? Have you ever wondered what the difference is between mobile banking and online banking? Even though the two terms are often used interchangeably, there are some variations between both services. Mobile banking is all about conducting banking transactions through an app on your smartphone or tablet. And online banking can be accessed through any internet-enabled device, including your laptop or desktop computer. Although both are convenient and accessible, mobile banking has become increasingly popular due to its portability. It offers all the features of online banking, plus an added layer of convenience. Benefits of mobile banking apps Mobile banking apps offer plenty of user-friendly benefits in addition to convenience and easy accessibility Enhanced user experience With intuitive design and easy-to-navigate interfaces, bank mobile apps make it easy for users to view their account balance and transaction history, track spending habits, and set up alerts for low account balances or upcoming bill payments. E-signing transactions E-signature is a game-changer in the banking industry, and mobile banking apps have embraced it. The use of e-signing transactions means no more waiting for paper checks or forms to be delivered by mail. You can now sign transactions electronically on your device, making the process faster and more efficient. Deposit checks at your convenience With mobile banking apps, visiting a bank branch or ATM to deposit checks is a thing of the past. Simply take a photo of the check through your phone's camera and deposit it using the app. This feature is not only convenient but also efficient and reduces the risk of losing or misplacing physical checks. Strengthened security features Mobile banking apps have advanced security features such as biometric login, two-factor authentication, and real-time fraud detection. These measures provide an extra layer of protection for your financial transactions and sensitive personal information. Monitor spending habits efficiently Check your balance at any time. On top of having quick access to your bank account, many mobile banking apps offer budgeting tools that help users track their expenses and identify areas where they can save money. This feature is especially helpful for those trying to stick to a budget or save for a specific goal. Easy bills payment A mobile banking app allows users to pay their bills—including utility, credit card, or mortgage payments—directly from their account without needing physical transactions. Payments can also be automated by setting the payment date and which account to debit. Fraud protection on the go In case of any suspicious activity on your account, a mobile banking app provides instant alerts and allows you to freeze or block your card immediately. With traditional banks, you may have to wait for business hours or visit a branch to report fraud. Around-the-clock customer support Instead of waiting for the typical weekday business hours, mobile banking platforms typically offer round-the-clock customer service resources. Many apps provide a range of support options, including live chat, email, and phone support. This continuous availability eliminates waiting for "business hours" to manage issues and provides users with peace of mind.
